name: Geohash encode, decode with bounding box, and eight neighbours
description: Encode latitude/longitude to a base-32 geohash of 1-20 characters, decode a geohash to its cell centre, half-size error and bounding box, or list its eight neighbouring cells (north clockwise to northwest).

provenance.metadata_source: public GitHub repository API (license field and created_at), observed this mining round; actual license file inspected
provenance.reference_values: Encode, neighbour and decode inputs are from upstream tests/test.js; five assert literal upstream strings or lists. All full outputs, including floats and bounding boxes, were generated by executing the pinned upstream main.js in Node, not this port; supplementary cases are labelled. reference/verify_upstream.py reruns upstream locally.

budget.enforcement: Raw CLI byte limit and POSIX alarm; strict schema, finite values and nesting checks; MCP subprocess killed/reaped after 10 seconds. One active calculation. Not a hostile-code sandbox.

limitations: WGS84-style latitude/longitude in degrees only by convention; the code is pure bisection on [-90, 90] x [-180, 180] and knows no datum. Lengths 1-20; integer geohash, auto precision from decimal strings, bounding-box coverage search and distance are not exposed. Neighbours near the poles are clamped to the pole latitude (as upstream), so they may repeat the input cell. A point exactly on a cell boundary goes to the lower/western cell because comparisons are strict.
port_notes: Port of encode, decode_bbox, decode, neighbors, ensure_valid_lon and ensure_valid_lat from main.js at the pinned commit: longitude-first bit interleaving, strict greater-than bisection, lower-case decode, neighbour offset of two half-errors and JavaScript % semantics (math.fmod) for longitude wrap. Invalid characters are rejected by schema instead of producing NaN.
